allowed_comments.body: FindSet is executed without SetLoadFields, so the loop loads the full Cust. Ledger Entry record even though it only needs Customer No., Open, and Remaining Amount; this creates avoidable I/O on potentially high-volume ledger data.
The parameter and local variables do not follow the project review convention: parameters require a p prefix and local variables require an underscore prefix.

This introduces a new table in the Microsoft base-application project using object ID 50200, despite the project configuration allowing changes to existing base-application objects rather than allocating a new object ID range.

This introduces a new page using object ID 50201 in the Microsoft base-application project; new object IDs are outside the stated change-existing-objects scope and will not be valid for this project without an approved range.

This introduces a new codeunit using object ID 50202 in the Microsoft base-application project; new object IDs are outside the stated change-existing-objects scope and require an approved object range.
Customer is read with FindFirst without SetLoadFields; this loads the full Customer record for a lookup that only uses Name. Select the required fields before the read.
The procedure parameter and local variable do not follow the project naming conventions: parameters require a p prefix and locals require an underscore prefix.
Setup tables are read with raw Get calls instead of the setup table GetRecordOnce caching pattern, causing repeated callers to issue unnecessary database reads.
The procedure parameters and local variables do not follow the project naming conventions: parameters require a p prefix and locals require an underscore prefix.
The procedure parameter and local variables do not follow the project naming conventions: parameters require a p prefix and locals require an underscore prefix.

OnAfterGetRecord executes a separate Permission.Count query for every permission-set row, creating an N+1 database pattern as the list grows. Replace the per-row count with a set-based/precomputed approach or cache the counts.

FindSet is used without SetLoadFields even though the loop reads only Document No. and Line No.; this causes full records to be loaded for every matching posted invoice line. Set the required fields before FindSet.
FindSet is used without SetLoadFields even though the loop reads only Quantity; this causes full records to be loaded for every matching posted invoice line. Set the required fields before FindSet.
Captions and tooltips are hardcoded user-facing strings instead of Labels, which prevents proper localization and violates the AL labeling convention.
The user-facing Message format is hardcoded rather than defined as a Label, so it cannot be localized consistently.
Local record variables use the project-inconsistent unprefixed naming convention; locals should use the required underscore prefix (for example, _PermissionSet and _DateComprRegister).
Procedure parameters and local record/total variables do not follow the required naming convention: parameters need a p prefix and locals need an underscore prefix.
The local Permission record variable does not use the required underscore prefix.
The new page and codeunits introduce application objects without corresponding permission-set entries in the working-tree changes, leaving access coverage undefined for the added objects.
The parameter does not follow the project's p-prefixed parameter convention (use pCompanyCode).
The local record variable does not follow the project's underscore-prefixed local-variable convention (use _FASetup).
The local record variable does not follow the project's underscore-prefixed local-variable convention (use _ReasonCode).
The parameter does not follow the project's p-prefixed parameter convention (use pCustomerNo).
The local record variable does not follow the project's underscore-prefixed local-variable convention (use _Customer).
The procedure parameters and local variables do not follow the project's required p/_ prefixes, making this new object inconsistent with the enforced AL naming conventions.
ParseAddressResponse is an internal procedure call but is invoked without the required this. self-reference.
LookupPostalAddress is an internal procedure call but is invoked without the required this. self-reference.

The new table has no permission-set entry granting access to table 50322. Without synchronized permissions, intended callers cannot reliably read or write this object; add it to the appropriate application permission set.

The new table has no permission-set entry granting access to table 50111. Without synchronized permissions, intended callers cannot reliably read or write this object; add it to the appropriate application permission set.
The new procedure parameters and local variables do not follow the project AL naming conventions: parameters should use the p prefix and locals should use the _ prefix.
KeyNotFoundErr is declared at object scope but is used only by RetrieveKey; declare this label in that procedure's local var block to avoid unnecessary global state.
Parameter names do not follow the repository AL convention: use pKeyName and pApiKey for procedure parameters.
The new page allocates object ID 50001, but this Microsoft base-application project must change existing objects rather than introduce objects in an unapproved ID range.
The new codeunit allocates object ID 50341, but this Microsoft base-application project must change existing objects rather than introduce objects in an unapproved ID range.
The new page has no corresponding permission-set change, so users will not receive explicit permissions to the page object.
The procedure parameters and local variable do not follow the project naming convention: parameters require a p prefix and locals require an underscore prefix.
The Enabled parameter does not follow the project naming convention; parameters require a p prefix.
The Vendor No. tooltip does not use the base application's standard tooltip for this mirrored field; use the standard number-series wording to preserve established UX and translations.
The Vendor Name tooltip differs from the base application's standard tooltip; use the standard wording to preserve established UX and translations.
The Vendor Balance (LCY) tooltip omits the standard explanation of the calculated completed-purchase value; use the base application's exact tooltip for this mirrored field.
The internal procedure call should use the required self-reference prefix: `this.IsCustomerNoFilled(CustomerNo)`.
PostedMsg is used only by GetPostingMessage and should be declared in that procedure's local var block rather than at object scope.
The procedure parameter and local record do not follow the project naming conventions: parameters require a `p` prefix and local variables require a leading `_`.
Object ID 50343 is outside the app's declared ID ranges (1-9999 and 12145-12146), so the app cannot compile with this object.
Object ID 50200 is outside the app's declared ID ranges (1-9999 and 12145-12146), so the app cannot compile with this object.
The parameter StartCount and local variable iCount do not follow the project's AL naming conventions; parameters require a p prefix and locals require an underscore prefix.
User-facing captions and tooltips are hardcoded string literals instead of localized labels, which prevents consistent translation and violates the project's AL review convention.
Procedure parameters do not follow the project naming convention requiring a p prefix (StatusCode and StatusName should be renamed to pStatusCode and pStatusName).
The display label is assembled with hardcoded user-facing text (' - '). Use a Label for the separator (with a placeholder comment if applicable) so the displayed value is localizable.
Procedure parameters do not follow the project naming convention requiring a p prefix (CustomerNo and CustomerName should be renamed to pCustomerNo and pCustomerName).
The procedure parameter and local record use nonconforming names; parameters must use the p prefix and local variables must use the _ prefix (pCustomerNo and _Customer).
Customer.Get is executed without SetLoadFields. Add SetLoadFields(Name) after applying filters and before the Get to avoid loading the full Customer record on this read path.
The TryFunction procedure repeats the nonconforming parameter and local variable names; use pCustomerNo and _Customer.
The procedure parameters and local variables do not follow project naming conventions; use p-prefixed parameters and _-prefixed locals (for example, pStartIndex, pLimitCount, _Index, and _Counter).
EchoCount uses a nonconforming parameter name; parameters must use the p prefix (pCountValue).

The tooltip for a field mirroring the base Customer field is not the base tooltip and uses a different, less precise description. Use the standard tooltip text to preserve consistent user guidance and localization.
The local record variable does not follow the repository AL naming convention for locals; use a leading underscore (for example, _Customer).

Customer.FindSet(true) runs over every matching customer without a preceding SetLoadFields call. This full-loads all Customer fields during the per-company upgrade; load at least Name and Search Name before FindSet to avoid unnecessary data transfer and memory use.
The local record and codeunit variables do not follow the project naming convention requiring an underscore prefix for locals (for example, _Customer and _UpgradeTag).
The event subscriber parameter does not follow the project convention requiring a p prefix for parameters; rename PerCompanyUpgradeTags to pPerCompanyUpgradeTags.
